    How it calculates

    Three steps, from the spec sheet to the shot.

    The same rules as i9’s room planner, so a camera you size here frames the same in the plan.

    1 · The angle at this zoom

    Makers publish the horizontal angle at the widest and the tightest end. In between, the calculator moves along the zoom on a log scale, which lands exactly on both published ends.

    tan(h/2) = tan(wide/2) × (tan(tele/2) ÷ tan(wide/2))^z

    2 · The frame at the person

    The width the camera sees at the person’s distance. Height follows the 16:9 picture.

    frame width = 2 × distance × tan(h/2)

    3 · The name of the shot

    A frame up to 0.75 m wide is a close-up, up to 1.25 m a medium close-up, up to 2.50 m a medium shot; wider is a wide shot.

    CU ≤ 0.75 m · MCU ≤ 1.25 m · MS ≤ 2.5 m

    Worked example

    Panasonic AW-UE20 (71° → 6°, 12×), 15 m (49 ft) from the pulpit. Full zoom: 2 × 15 × tan(3°) = 1.57 m (5.2 ft), a medium shot. A 0.6 m close-up needs 0.6 m ÷ (2 × tan(3°)) = 5.72 m or closer.

    PTZ distance questions.

    Close-up range, the formula, zoom and shot names.

    How far can a PTZ camera be for a close-up?

    It depends on its tele angle. With a close-up framed 2 ft · 0.6 m across, a 12× Panasonic AW-UE20 reaches 19 ft, a 20× Canon CR-N300 31 ft and a 24× Panasonic UE50 34 ft.

    How do you calculate a PTZ camera’s field of view at a distance?

    Frame width = 2 × distance × tan(horizontal angle ÷ 2). The calculator takes the wide and tele angles from the maker’s spec page and works out every zoom position in between.

    Does the calculator use digital zoom?

    No. It uses the optical zoom range only, from the maker’s published angles. Digital zoom or cropping a 4K picture tightens the shot further, at a cost in sharpness.

    What do CU, MCU, MS and WS mean?

    Close-up (head and shoulders), medium close-up (chest up), medium shot (waist up) and wide shot. The calculator names the shot from the frame width at the person, with the same limits as i9’s room planner.

    Is the distance measured along the floor?

    Measure the straight line from the lens to the person. For a camera high on a back wall, that is a little longer than the floor distance.
